clue.text: It's testing to keep the standard up

definitions.text: It's testing to keep the standard up

parts.words: It's testing to keep the standard up
parts.note: a plain description of the routine checking a factory does on its products so that their level never slips

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a trial exists to maintain a benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial inspection of goods to maintain their grade is exactly what this business phrase names.

clue.text: Having made considerable profit from the tobacco evil?

parts.note: a quid is a lump of chewing tobacco
sin means wickedness or evil

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person has got rich from the wicked weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quids in' is British slang for being well in profit; a quid is also slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quids in is British slang for having come out of a deal well ahead financially.

clue.text: I, loner, left out, with hard act to follow, possibly

definitions.text: I, loner, left out, with hard act to follow, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters gathered here might be arranged some other way
left out says the letter standing for left is dropped from the word loner

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solitary person says they were excluded and face following a tough performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes L (left) from LONER, giving ONER; I, ONER, H and ACT are shuffled by 'possibly'. The whole clue also describes the answer, a religious recluse.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious hermit who lives withdrawn from the world is a loner who has left society out.

clue.text: Family concern

definitions.meaning: children or offspring, as in dying without children
a matter of concern or a topic under dispute

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both offspring, as in a will, and a matter under debate or worry.

clue.text: Leisure centre not available in the Middle Ages?

definitions.text: Leisure centre not available in the Middle Ages?

parts.words: Leisure centre not available in the Middle Ages?
parts.note: read not as medieval history but as middle age in a life: a recreation venue for teenagers is closed to the middle-aged

explanation.surface: A history question about whether medieval people had sports facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle Ages' suggests the medieval period; it means people in middle age, who are too old for a club meant for teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: A club for teenagers' leisure is by definition not open to people in middle age.

clue.text: See 1 across
Swindler caught holding most of pile

indicators.note: holding says the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: ct is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: most of says the final letter of the synonym is lost

parts.note: a pile is a heap

explanation.surface: A con man is arrested while clutching the bulk of his fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like the arrest in the story, but cricket scorecards shorten it; 'most of' leaves HEA and 'holding' sets it between those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat is a swindler, someone who gains by deceit.

clue.text: Number puzzle? That's easy!

parts.note: a problem is a puzzle to be solved

explanation.surface: Someone shown a numerical puzzle shrugs that it is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of easy assent, saying a task gives no difficulty at all.

clue.text: Girl associated with drink got up about one

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A young woman, linked to the bottle, got out of bed for one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea, so the girl is linked with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a girl's name, tied to a drink through the rhyming slang Rosie Lee for tea.

clue.text: Dud tile is cracked, but one's not in favour of the new technology

definitions.text: one's not in favour of the new technology

indicators.note: a cracked tile is broken, so the letters of these words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A faulty broken tile and a person who dislikes modern gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: The term began with nineteenth-century machine-breakers and now means anyone opposed to new technology.

clue.text: It helps one to hear the organ piece

definitions.meaning: a small bone in the middle ear that passes on sound vibrations
one part of the ear, the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Something aids hearing, namely a passage of organ music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ piece' suggests music; the organ is the ear and the piece one of its bones.
explanation.definitionFit: This anvil-shaped bone in the middle ear transmits sound and is a component of the hearing organ.

clue.text: Expounds in confusion about energy not made public

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the next piece
confusion means the letters of the word Expounds are muddled up

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone explains muddledly about energy matters kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' rearranges EXPOUNDS to UNXPOSED, and 'about' places it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept hidden from public view or knowledge is unrevealed, a close synonym.

clue.text: Little bird worried cat. Honest!

indicators.note: worried means troubled or shaken up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a cat really did harass a small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonechat is a small European songbird of the thrush family.

clue.text: Manuscript marks from old boy, Samuel's teacher

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
in the Bible the boy Samuel was raised and taught by the priest Eli

explanation.surface: Notes in a document come from a former pupil and the prophet's mentor.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is a dagger-shaped symbol used in old manuscripts to mark doubtful passages; the plural is wanted.

clue.text: 'Green' backing for French resort

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the resort's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Evian-les-Bains is a French spa town on Lake Geneva

explanation.surface: A green campaign gains support for a French spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like environmentalism; it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or unsophisticated, a sense shared by this word.

clue.text: Found form

definitions.meaning: to found is to set up or create an institution
to form is likewise to bring into being

explanation.definitionFit: To set up something lasting is both to found it and to form it.

clue.text: Suddenly starts attacking and thus allows freedom

definitions.meaning: to unleash a sudden assault, as in lashing out at someone

explanation.surface: An attacker launches a sudden offensive and so frees people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to unleash an attack and to set something free from restraint.

clue.text: Heretic to waver, having no practical experience

indicators.note: waver means to sway unsteadily, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A dissenter starts to wobble, lacking any hands-on experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is part of the letters shuffled, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretic means based on theory alone rather than practice.

clue.text: Casual type, but he's improving

parts.note: describes a handyman taking occasional work who makes repairs and improvements around the house

explanation.surface: A laid-back person is nonetheless getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casual' suggests relaxed, but means occasional work; 'improving' means making home improvements, not getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman doing occasional work fixes and improves homes, the phrase's sense.

clue.text: Fit to pick first, as those standing should be

indicators.note: first says the second piece of the clue goes in front

parts.note: to elect is to pick by vote
fit means able or capable

explanation.surface: An election note says candidates should be fit to be picked first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' means standing for election, so candidates should be choosable.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates standing for office should be capable of being chosen by voters.

clue.text: Clip could show it set on one side

definitions.meaning: a notch clipped in an animal's ear to show ownership
to reserve or allocate for a purpose

explanation.surface: A cut might reveal something reserved for later.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an ownership notch in livestock's ear and, as a verb, setting funds aside.

clue.text: The writer's party with Cape wine

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter as me, the 's meaning has
a do is a party
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: The setter holds a party with South African wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape wine' looks like South African wine, but Cape gives only C.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux wine from the Médoc region of France.

clue.text: Revolutionary way, they say, for smoke

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: they say means the next word is given by its pronunciation

parts.note: a route is a way

explanation.surface: A rebel's road leads, people claim, to a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, something to smoke.

clue.text: Greek character, a doctor, produces the shape

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A Greek letter and a physician together produce a geometrical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb is a rhombus, an equilateral parallelogram.

clue.text: Charge in connection with TV?

definitions.meaning: switched on, as a television set is, read as two words

explanation.surface: A price is levied for television.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits into two words: switched on, as with a TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means an attack, while the split phrase describes a television that is switched on.

clue.text: Although in a spin, I provide stability

definitions.text: Although in a spin, I provide stability

parts.words: Although in a spin, I provide stability
parts.note: describes a spinning wheel device whose rotation keeps instruments steady, though the phrase in a spin usually means flustered

explanation.surface: A flustered person still claims to be the steady one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a spin' suggests panic; here it means literally rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: This rotating device resists changes to its axis and so steadies compasses and craft.

clue.text: Make a face about a bit of corn

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to grin is to make a face, a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face over a piece of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain is a single seed or kernel of a cereal crop.

clue.text: Brush around the garden feature

indicators.note: around means the letters of the word Brush are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sweeping round a feature in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant, a typical feature of a garden.

clue.text: At sea, a salt is an adversary

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, a sailor turns out to be an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: A salt is an old sailor, which fits 'At sea' in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker, so an adversary.

clue.text: Wild mob after the gunners, showing its brutal character

indicators.note: after says the jumbled piece comes behind the gunners

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters of mob run riot

explanation.surface: An unruly crowd trails the artillery, revealing its violent nature.
explanation.walkthrough: Rambo is the violent hero of the 1980s action films.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambo is the brutal film commando whose name stands for any violently aggressive person.

clue.text: Those 'downstairs' having influence?

parts.note: suggests servants below stairs in a big house, but means an informal group of close advisers wielding power

explanation.surface: Asks whether the household staff below stairs hold sway.
explanation.walkthrough: In grand British houses the kitchen and servants were downstairs; the phrase names a leader's informal advisers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a political leader's informal circle of private advisers, as opposed to the official ministers.

clue.text: See 27
